transcript.statement: The Trustworthiness dimension is critical for ensuring the security and privacy of user data within the Autonomous Driving System. Requirements TRU-01 (data encryption) and TRU-02 (role-based access control) are essential for protecting sensitive information from unauthorized access. TRU-03 (auditability) ensures accountability in data handling, while TRU-04 (data anonymization) safeguards user identities. Regular security audits (TRU-05) and secure remote updates (TRU-06) are crucial for maintaining system integrity. Lastly, TRU-07 emphasizes user awareness regarding data usage, fostering trust in the system.

conflicts_raised.description: Requiring end-to-end data encryption (TRU-01) might conflict with prioritizing smoothness during emergency maneuvers (EFF-07), as encryption could introduce latency affecting real-time responsiveness.

transcript.statement: The Sustainability dimension is vital for reducing energy consumption and minimizing the carbon footprint of the Autonomous Driving System. Requirements GRN-01 (energy optimization), GRN-02 (renewable energy), GRN-03 (lifecycle assessments), GRN-04 (energy recovery efficiency), GRN-05 (carbon emissions monitoring), GRN-06 (energy-efficient routing), and GRN-07 (emergency energy protocols) collectively ensure that the system operates in an environmentally responsible manner. These requirements not only support global sustainability goals but also enhance the public perception of the autonomous vehicle technology.

conflicts_raised.description: Optimizing for a 30% reduction in travel time (EFF-01) may conflict with energy consumption goals (GRN-01), as faster routes could lead to higher energy use.
Prioritizing smoothness during emergency maneuvers (EFF-07) may hinder energy-efficient routing algorithms (GRN-06), potentially increasing energy consumption.

transcript.statement: The Responsibility dimension is essential for ensuring that the Autonomous Driving System complies with regulations and operates ethically. Requirements RES-01 (compliance with safety reports), RES-02 (multi-layer safety architecture), RES-03 (Minimal Risk Maneuvers), RES-04 (monitoring ODD), RES-05 (HMI warnings), RES-06 (prioritizing safety over comfort during emergencies), and RES-07 (documenting decisions for accountability) collectively ensure that the system upholds accountability and fairness. These requirements are crucial for maintaining public trust and ensuring that the system operates within legal and ethical boundaries.

conflicts_raised.description: Both requirements mandate executing Minimal Risk Maneuvers within 5 seconds upon detecting a critical failure, leading to potential conflicts in prioritization between safety and performance.

Prioritizing passenger safety over comfort during emergency maneuvers (RES-06) may contradict the requirement to prioritize smoothness during such maneuvers (EFF-07), creating a conflict in operational strategies.

transcript.statement: Performance Efficiency is crucial for the Autonomous Driving System to operate effectively in real-time scenarios. Requirements EFF-01 (30% travel time reduction) and EFF-04 (100ms latency for ODD monitoring) ensure quick responses while maximizing throughput. EFF-02 (jerk below 0.5 m/s³) is essential for passenger comfort, and EFF-05 (95% success in speed profile generation) guarantees reliability. EFF-06 (50ms for obstacle handling) supports responsiveness, while EFF-07 (prioritizing smoothness) is vital during emergencies to maintain passenger comfort. However, conflicts arise with Safety and Green dimensions regarding smoothness and energy usage during critical maneuvers.

transcript.statement: The Safety dimension is paramount for the Autonomous Driving System, ensuring that safety mechanisms are robust and effective. Requirement SAF-01 establishes a multi-layer safety architecture for comprehensive hazard mitigation. SAF-02 mandates a Minimal Risk Maneuver within 5 seconds, crucial for fault tolerance. SAF-03 ensures continuous ODD monitoring, while SAF-04 and SAF-05 prioritize passenger comfort and vehicle stability during operations. SAF-06 guarantees quick handling of obstacles, and SAF-07 allows for an emergency protocol to relax smoothness constraints when necessary. This flexibility is essential for maintaining safety during critical maneuvers.

requirements.text: The system shall implement a multi-layer safety architecture ensuring robust collision protection and fail-safe operations.
The system shall execute a Minimal Risk Maneuver within 5 seconds upon detecting critical failures to ensure safety and performance.
The system shall continuously monitor Operational Design Domain compliance and issue human takeover requests when boundaries are approached.
The system shall maintain jerk below 0.5 m/s³ during normal operation while allowing smoothness adjustments during emergencies.
The system shall satisfy curvature constraints to prevent rollover during maneuvers at all speeds.
The system shall utilize iterative quadratic programming to handle non-convex obstacle constraints with a response time under 50 milliseconds.
The system shall implement lightweight encryption during emergencies without compromising responsiveness.
The system shall establish protocols for smoothness adjustments that minimize energy consumption during emergencies.
The system shall document all safety and compliance-related decisions for accountability and regulatory purposes.
